Definition: to undulate (as the earth, the sky, etc.; also a field of grain), particularly through fear; specifically, to spring (as a locust)
BiblicalUsage: To quake or shake — the earth, the heavens, the sea. David sang that the earth shook and trembled when God came down in anger, and Haggai promises, 'Yet once, it is a little while, and I will shake the heavens, and the earth, and the sea, and the dry land.'
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the shaking is God's signature on history: what can be shaken will be shaken, so that what cannot be shaken remains.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
